parsed.explanation: Thin-data, structurally benign-but-unprotective jurisdiction: no trans-specific criminal offence, no documented targeting, some sexual-orientation protections and a UN-statement signature as climate signals. Offsetting exposures: no gender recognition means a passport/presentation mismatch follows the traveller into every document check with no domestic remedy, and no legal or social record tells us how officials handle it. General LGBTQ stigmatisation is documented but not trans-specific. Per rule 13, this resolves above the criminalising structural tier and below any acceptance-with-protections tier: the worst documented feature is an open question (how officials treat document mismatch) plus a thin-recourse environment, not a known exposure. Incidents absence is not safety evidence, but nothing documented elevates severity. Minors travelling with a guardian face the same document-mismatch and no-recourse profile; no age-dependent trans rule is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: No marker-change procedure exists; a mismatched passport/presentation is visible at every border, immigration and hotel check with no domestic remedy, and no policy says how such cases are handled.
entry_documents.protection: No entry bar or scrutiny rule targeting trans visitors is documented; UN joint-statement signature is a climate signal only.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch is the primary discovery vector; consequence of discovery is undocumented, so severity cannot be resolved upward or downward.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No trans-specific arrest, detention or custody-placement evidence exists; how a discovered trans detainee would be placed is unknown.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If any interaction with police occurred, hate-crime enhancement covers sexual orientation only, not gender identity.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility-access rule (baths, wards, dorms) is recorded either way; mismatch-driven ward placement if injured is an open question.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No documented interaction between facility rules and document regime.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No refusal-of-care or HRT-import evidence either way.
care_services.protection: Labour-code discrimination ban reaches only employment and names sexual orientation only.
care_services.interaction: A trans visitor would have to squeeze a care refusal into a sexual-orientation ground that does not on its face fit.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: General LGBTQ stigmatisation among the population is documented but not trans-specific; no state threat-framing, profiling or enforcement practice is recorded.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: No police practice bearing on trans people is documented at all.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No age-dependent trans rule; unresolved age-of-consent (16 vs 18) is a secondary, sexuality-law factor the guardian should assume at 18.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's guardian faces the same document-mismatch regime on the minor's papers.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented. No trans-specific violence recorded; absence reflects no monitoring, not safety.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime sentencing enhancement excludes gender identity; police response to anti-trans violence is unknown.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: General LGBTQ stigma could colour police reception of a trans complainant; undocumented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination ground beyond employment; nothing reaches housing, services or accommodation; no trans-named protection machinery exists.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Only the penal-code sentencing enhancement and labour-code ban, both sexual-orientation-only.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Whether those provisions have ever been interpreted to cover trans people is unsourced.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra has a documented, universal, state-run visitor-facing restriction (registration/exclusion). This dossier documents no such rule — only a passive document mismatch with no hostile enforcement shown. Structurally above 0.35: no state exposure is documented.

Kestrel Isles documents actual secondary screening and refusals of trans visitors. Here no such enforcement is documented; the mismatch exposure exists on paper but no practice is recorded, so severity is less documented than 0.55-B — slightly above, since the unknown cannot outrank a documented pattern.

Meridia documents trained officers, appeal tribunals and release-after-detention remedies. This jurisdiction documents no protective machinery at all and general LGBTQ stigma. It sits clearly below 0.75: protections are thinner and the social climate signal is worse.

Vellmaris shows working national equality law, complaint remedies and court-ordered release. Here protections do not name gender identity and remedies are thin, but no hostile enforcement is documented — structurally between the 0.65 and 0.45 tiers.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is one of absence rather than hostility: no criminal statute touching trans visitors, no documented targeting by police or border officers, and thin but non-hostile climate signals (decriminalisation since 2012, employment discrimination ban, UN-statement signature). The one continuous traveller-facing exposure is structural: with no marker-change procedure anywhere, a presenting/identity mismatch is visible at every document check and no domestic policy or remedy governs what follows. Because the dossier documents no enforcement, no incident, and no hostile official practice, that exposure remains an open question rather than a known harm, and per rule 13 an unanswered question cannot out-vote the documented absence of criminalisation. But general LGBTQ stigmatisation, gender-identity-blind protections, and thin sourcing prevent this from rising toward the acceptance-with-protections tier. Minors add no distinct documented exposure beyond the same mismatch regime. Net placement: reduced-risk band, mid-band, pending any evidence of how officials treat discovered mismatches.
